header.title: P.Oxy. 79 5205: Spell for the Chariot Race: AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Greek magical papyri and amulets
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's urn:magic:ddbdp:372070:grc, from papyri.info's Digital Corpus of Literary Papyri (CC BY 3.0), one English line for each line of the original. Only some passages are translated so far: those that the Atlas of Ancient Myth, Magic in the Ancient Texts and the demons-and-angels study cite.
header.statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.

notes.3: Sarakenos, Belhmou, Parthaon, Didyme, Nymphike, Pele. and Strabos look like the names of the Blues' horses (Καλλάϊνοι, 'the Blues', in line 5), and are kept as they stand; Belhmou is written with a Coptic letter (ϩ). Many letters are dotted as doubtful, and lines 7 and 14 to 16 are largely illegible; dots stand for unread letters. 'Corpse-[daemon]' renders the restored νεκ[ύδαιμον]. In line 8 the preposition κα|τά is broken across the line; 'by' is given in line 8. The angel names in line 10 may be the names sworn by or those addressed. In line 10 'i.[' (ι.[) might be the start of 'hippodrome', but it is lost. Ousirapis (Osiris-Apis), Ousor and Ouser (Osiris) and Mneuis (the Mnevis bull) are Egyptian divine names. 'Make fall' renders πτωματίζω.
